newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Chubu Commodity Exchange to list oil futures.
newsitem.headline: Japan Chubu Commodity Exchange to list oil futures.

text.p: Chubu Commodity Exchange in Nagoya, central Japan, said on Tuesday it plans to list gasoline, gas oil and kerosene futures contracts by April 1999.

"We are planning to apply for government approval next summer and to list the three futures contracts as early as April 1999," Hideaki Nakamura, head of the exchange's planning department, told Reuters.
He said the contracts are likely to be yen-denominated and one lot is expected to be equivalent to 10 kilolitres.
Other details of the contracts, including the specifications of the oil products and delivery locations, will be decided by early next year by a panel set up by the exchange, he added.
Nakamura said that the exchange is unlikely to list crude oil futures after the oil product listing, partly because Nagoya, unlike Tokyo, has no physical crude oil market.
"It would probably be Tokyo's (the Tokyo Commodity Exchange's) job to list crude oil futures," he said.
The Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM) said in May it plans to list either crude oil or gasoline in 1999 as its first-ever energy futures contract.
Nakamura said the oil product futures contracts are expected to be traded actively as the region has a sufficient number of oil traders with hedging needs, as well as speculators.
"Enough speculators -- that's what we have, and what Singapore doesn't," said Nakamura, who visited the Singapore International Monetary Exchange (SIMEX) in June.

SIMEX's Brent crude oil futures contract has been dogged by poor trading volume since it was first listed in 1995, trading only a few hundred lots per day compared with 40,000 to 60,000 on London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE).
The industrial city of Nagoya on the Pacific coast is one of Japan's major oil product trading centres, with active spot trading and five refineries in the region.
